params.script_inline:
import sys, json, uuid, datetime

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
# Which leg of the walk this hop is. The key is the porter's own, so the phase
# words of the lanes that were here first can never collide with it.
phase = str(ctx.get("port_phase", ""))
op = hop.get("operation")
err = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")
# The correlation key of ONE transfer. On the export walk it names the run; on
# an import it doubles as the `port_scratch` key the part and the probe result
# meet under, because a code cell holds no state between hops and the store
# cannot return two result sets at once.
run = str(ctx.get("port_run", ""))
table_ctx = str(ctx.get("port_table", ""))
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")

# ---------------------------------------------------------- WHOSE DOCUMENT
# The hive this porter speaks for. It is the name of the directory its store
# writes its seed set into, and it is stamped into every import part -- which is
# what keeps two hives that both have a table called `entities` out of each
# other's seed set (GH #471, GH #555).
HIVE = "affinity"
# The document format. A version, because a document outlives the code that
# wrote it: a reader that does not know this string refuses instead of guessing,
# and an importer that meets an unknown one says so on the reject lane.
FORMAT = "meclaw-affinity-export/1"
# The lane to this hive's own store, and the notepad table inside it.
STORE_ROUTE = "astore"
SCRATCH = "port_scratch"

# ------------------------------------------------------- SCHEMA MIRROR (#471)
# Byte mirror of `templates/affinity/store/config.json` -- THAT file is the
# authority, this is the copy a script can carry (a script cannot import), minus
# the machine table and plus the two tables the store creates itself from
# `params.canonical`. `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh471_the_porters_mirror_their_stores.rs`
# compares the two and is red the moment a column is added to a store without
# being added here, which is the only way a transfer can silently start dropping
# a column.
#
# `port_scratch` is excluded on purpose and this is a decision, not an omission:
# it is this lane's own notepad, the place one import part and the probe result
# meet. Carrying it over would restart another hive's half-finished import in a
# colony that never had one.
#
# The FTS shadow tables are excluded for a second reason: the store rebuilds
# them from `params.fts` when it wakes, so they are a derived index rather than
# something the source decided.
SCHEMA = {
    "entity_aliases": {
        "alias": "text",
        "canonical": "text",
        "recorded_at": "text"
    },
    "entity_rejected_pairs": {
        "left_value": "text",
        "right_value": "text",
        "recorded_at": "text"
    },
    "entities": {
        "entity_id": "text",
        "kind": "text",
        "display_name": "text",
        "canonical_name": "text",
        "owner_member": "text",
        "aieos": "json",
        "aieos_version": "text",
        "mx": "json",
        "status": "text",
        "supersedes": "text",
        "source": "text",
        "confidence": "int",
        "recorded_at": "text"
    },
    "relations": {
        "id": "text",
        "src": "text",
        "dst": "text",
        "kind": "text",
        "weight": "int",
        "valid_from": "text",
        "valid_until": "text",
        "source": "text",
        "evidence": "json",
        "status": "text",
        "recorded_at": "text"
    },
    "trust": {
        "id": "text",
        "entity_id": "text",
        "audience": "text",
        "level": "text",
        "decided_by": "text",
        "decided_at": "text"
    },
    "disclosure": {
        "id": "text",
        "entity_id": "text",
        "field_path": "text",
        "audience": "text",
        "mode": "text",
        "decided_at": "text",
        "audience_set": "json"
    },
    "subscribers": {
        "id": "text",
        "cell_path": "text",
        "subject": "text",
        "audience": "text",
        "channel": "text",
        "slots": "json",
        "pack_hash": "text",
        "status": "text",
        "sent_at": "text"
    },
    "proposals": {
        "id": "text",
        "source_ref": "text",
        "entity_ref": "text",
        "field_path": "text",
        "value": "json",
        "status": "text",
        "decided_by": "text",
        "decided_at": "text",
        "recorded_at": "text",
        "supersedes": "text"
    },
    "audit": {
        "id": "text",
        "at": "text",
        "actor": "text",
        "action": "text",
        "subject": "text",
        "outcome": "text",
        "reason_code": "text",
        "detail": "json"
    }
}
# ------------------------------------------------------ /SCHEMA MIRROR (#471)

# The order of the document, and it is load-bearing on the way IN: the two
# store-owned identity tables come FIRST, so that by the time `entities` rows are
# inserted the alias table they derive `canonical_name` from is already there. A
# document applied in this order needs no repair; one applied in any other order
# is repaired by the `canonicalize` the final part triggers.
WALK = ["entity_aliases", "entity_rejected_pairs", "entities", "relations", "trust", "disclosure", "subscribers", "proposals", "audit"]

# What makes a row THE SAME row across two hives. An import inserts a row whose
# key it does not already carry and skips one it does -- that, and nothing else,
# is what makes the same document applied twice leave the same state.
KEYS = {"entities": ["entity_id"], "relations": ["id"], "trust": ["id"], "disclosure": ["id"], "subscribers": ["id"], "proposals": ["id"], "audit": ["id"]}
# The identity dimensions the STORE keys itself, as `[table, column]`. They are
# never inserted: `set_alias` and `reject_pair` are upserts on a real PRIMARY
# KEY, so applying such a part twice is arithmetic.
ALIAS_DIM = {"entity_aliases": ["entities", "display_name"]}
REJECT_DIM = {"entity_rejected_pairs": ["entities", "display_name"]}
CANON = [["entities", "display_name"]]

# The columns whose LOSS in transit would launder a row. An import refuses a
# part for one of these tables whose declared schema does not carry them -- an
# imported disclosure decision whose audience did not survive is a decision that
# may be read as applying to anyone.
PROVENANCE = {"disclosure": ["audience", "audience_set"], "trust": ["audience"], "subscribers": ["audience"]}

# STORE-OWNED derived columns. They travel in the document (a backup that cannot
# be diffed against the store it came from is not a backup) but they are stripped
# before insert: the store derives them from the alias table, which travels too,
# so the identity an entity had in the source hive is REPRODUCED rather than
# asserted.
#
# RESET is the other half, and it is a different decision. `pack_hash` and
# `sent_at` do not say what the source DECIDED, they say what the source already
# DELIVERED -- to a cell path in a colony that no longer exists. Carried over,
# the receiving push lane compares the fresh pack against a hash it never sent
# and stays silent for ever (`templates/affinity/push/config.json`), so a reborn
# member would never deliver its first identity pack. The subscribe decision
# itself -- who, which slots, which channel, active or not -- travels untouched.
DERIVED = {"entities": ["canonical_name"]}
RESET = {"subscribers": ["pack_hash", "sent_at"]}
# What the refusal says when a part names a table this hive will not take.
NOT_TRANSFERABLE = "`port_scratch` is this lane's own notepad and the FTS shadow tables are rebuilt when the store wakes -- neither is curated record."

def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park():
    emit([])


def store_op(args, ph, table=""):
    return {"header": {"route": STORE_ROUTE, "phase": ph, "port_run": run,
                       "port_table": table},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "p-" + ph,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)}]}


def store_slot(args, ph):
    """One `transfer` slot addressed at this hive's own store (R-0904-3).

    The slot is a TOP-LEVEL body key rather than a tool call, because the
    substrate answers it BEFORE `handle()` -- there is no store op that could
    do this and there never was. `messages` travels empty beside it: this
    cell's own `emits` requires the slot to be present, and an export that said
    something here would be this cell claiming a sentence about a document it
    never read.
    """
    return {"header": {"route": STORE_ROUTE, "phase": ph, "port_run": run,
                       "port_table": ""},
            "messages": [],
            "transfer": args}


def refuse(reason, text):
    """The transfer path's fail-closed exit.

    Nothing has been written when this fires on the ingress hop, and the caller
    gets a reason it can read on a lane the level above drains. The header
    carries the same key set as the two success lanes plus the reason, so a
    parent edge can promote it on either lane without a missing key making its
    CEL modifier fail (a failed modifier skips the whole edge).
    """
    emit([{"header": {"route": "reject", "reject_reason": reason,
                      "port_run": run, "port_table": table_ctx},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "p-reject",
                         "text": text}]}])


def rows_of(dd):
    msgs = dd.get("messages", [])
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        payload = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text", "[]"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    return payload if isinstance(payload, list) else []


def first_text(dd):
    for m in dd.get("messages", []):
        if m.get("text"):
            return m.get("text")
    return ""


def key_of(row, cols):
    return "\x1e".join(str(row.get(c, "") or "") for c in cols)


def order_of(table):
    if table in ALIAS_DIM:
        return ["alias"]
    if table in REJECT_DIM:
        return ["left_value", "right_value"]
    return KEYS.get(table) or sorted(SCHEMA[table].keys())[:1]


# ============================================================ EXPORT (out)
#
# The store writes its own seed set, and this cell only says where (GH #555,
# ruling R-0904-3: *"cells manage their own files, nobody else does"*). Until
# 0.29.0 this leg walked every table through a message of its own into a sink
# cell two levels up, which is how a document that is a FILE by definition came
# to travel as a stack of messages. The `transfer` slot writes
# `<fence>/<dir>/seed/<table>.jsonl` itself -- the very format a hive is born
# from -- bounded by the fence the STORE declares for itself
# (`params.transfer.base_path`). What is left here is the walk ORDER, which is
# this hive's knowledge and nobody else's, and the completion word.


# The store's answer to the slot. It is a DIRECT reply -- the substrate
# addresses it at this cell instead of routing it through the hive's edges --
# so no `set_context` modifier runs on the way and the hop is the whole of what
# it says. That is why this branch is keyed on the operation and not on a phase
# word: there is no store op called `export`, so the name is unambiguous.
if op == "export":
    if err:
        refuse("export_write_failed",
               "export aborted: the store would not write its seed set (%s: %s). No marker was "
               "written, so the directory is not a document -- and a prefix looks complete to "
               "whoever imports it" % (err, first_text(d)))
    try:
        written_doc = json.loads(first_text(d) or "{}")
    except Exception:
        written_doc = {}
    if not isinstance(written_doc, dict):
        written_doc = {}
    rows_total = 0
    for n in (written_doc.get("rows") or {}).values():
        try:
            rows_total += int(n)
        except Exception:
            pass
    emit([{"header": {"route": "export_done", "export_hive": HIVE,
                      "seed_dir": str(written_doc.get("seed_dir") or ""),
                      "export_of": len(written_doc.get("tables") or []),
                      "rows_written": rows_total,
                      "port_run": run, "port_table": ""},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "p-export",
                         "text": first_text(d)}]}])


if phase == "export":
    # `hop.export_to` is the run's own directory when the caller named one (the
    # operator passes it through the way it passes `hop.target`). Under it each
    # holder keeps a directory of its OWN name: `memory-hive` and `affinity`
    # both have a table called `entities`, and one shared directory would write
    # one over the other without a word (GH #471).
    dest = str(hop.get("export_to", "") or "").strip("/")
    emit([store_slot({"operation": "export",
                      "to": (dest + "/" + HIVE) if dest else HIVE,
                      "tables": WALK}, "export-file")])


# ============================================================ IMPORT (in)

def receipt(part, written):
    return {"header": {"route": "dump", "port_run": run,
                       "port_hive": HIVE, "port_table": part["table"],
                       "export_part": part.get("part", 0),
                       "export_of": part.get("of", 0),
                       "export_final": "1" if part.get("final") else "0",
                       "rows_written": written},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                          "text": json.dumps({"format": FORMAT, "table": part["table"],
                                              "export_id": part.get("export_id", ""),
                                              "rows_in_part": len(part.get("rows") or []),
                                              "rows_written": written,
                                              "imported_at": now})}]}


def canon_ops():
    """Re-derive every identity dimension this hive keys from the alias tables
    the document carried. Runs once, on the FINAL part: by then every alias the
    source hive had judged is in this store, so a row inserted before its alias
    arrived catches up. A hive that keys no identity dimension has nothing to
    re-derive and this is the empty list."""
    return [store_op({"operation": "canonicalize", "table": t, "column": col},
                     "import-applied", t) for t, col in CANON]


def check_part(part):
    """Everything that must be true BEFORE a single row is written."""
    if not isinstance(part, dict) or part.get("format") != FORMAT:
        refuse("import_format",
               "import refused: the body is not a %s part. A document format is a version, "
               "and a reader that guesses at an unknown one writes rows nobody declared" % FORMAT)
    table = str(part.get("table") or "")
    if table not in SCHEMA:
        refuse("import_unknown_table",
               "import refused: %r is not a transferable table of this hive. %s"
               % (table, NOT_TRANSFERABLE))
    declared = part.get("schema")
    if not isinstance(declared, dict):
        refuse("import_schema_drift",
               "import refused: the part for %s carries no schema header. The header is what "
               "makes a part readable without this code -- a row list alone is a guess" % table)
    unknown = sorted(set(declared) - set(SCHEMA[table]))
    if unknown:
        refuse("import_schema_drift",
               "import refused: the part for %s declares column(s) %s this hive does not have. "
               "The source is newer than this store; growing the schema is a template change, "
               "not something an import may do silently" % (table, ", ".join(unknown)))
    # The provenance gate. A part that lost a disclosure-governing column in
    # transit is refused whole: a row whose audience did not survive is a row
    # that may be told to anyone, and an audience cannot be reconstructed
    # afterwards by anybody. An audience that is present but EMPTY is written as
    # it stands -- empty means invisible, which is the honest fate of such a row,
    # and inventing one would be the laundering itself.
    for col in PROVENANCE.get(table, []):
        if col not in declared:
            refuse("missing_audience" if col.startswith("audience") else "missing_channel",
                   "import refused: the part for %s does not carry %r. Provenance is never "
                   "reconstructed and never guessed -- an untagged import is a row that may "
                   "be told to anyone" % (table, col))
    rows = part.get("rows")
    if not isinstance(rows, list):
        refuse("import_format",
               "import refused: the part for %s has no rows array" % table)
    return table, rows


def rows_for_insert(table, rows):
    """Strip what the store owns, keep what the source DECIDED.

    Derived identity columns go (the store re-derives them from the transferred
    alias tables); the columns in RESET are blanked, because they record what
    THIS installation already did rather than what the source decided, and a
    delivery stamp carried into a colony that never made the delivery suppresses
    the first one. Every other column, provenance first, is copied byte for byte.
    Nothing here defaults, fills in or intersects -- an audience was decided when
    the row was written, and an import that recomputed it would be re-deciding
    what a transfer must carry.
    """
    drop = set(DERIVED.get(table, []))
    blank = set(RESET.get(table, []))
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        row = {k: ("" if k in blank else v) for k, v in r.items() if k not in drop}
        out.append(row)
    return out


if phase == "import":
    run = "import:" + str(uuid.uuid4())
    try:
        part = json.loads(first_text(d) or "null")
    except Exception:
        part = None
    if part is None:
        refuse("import_format",
               "import refused: the body carries no readable %s part" % FORMAT)
    # Named before it is validated, so a refusal can say WHICH part it refused.
    table_ctx = str(part.get("table") or "") if isinstance(part, dict) else ""
    table, rows = check_part(part)
    final = bool(part.get("final"))

    # An ABSENT part transfers nothing by definition -- it is the source hive
    # saying it never had the table. Still a receipt, and still the re-derivation
    # if it happens to be the last one.
    if part.get("absent") or not rows:
        emit((canon_ops() if final else []) + [receipt(part, 0)])

    if table in ALIAS_DIM:
        dim = ALIAS_DIM[table]
        ops = [store_op({"operation": "set_alias", "table": dim[0], "column": dim[1],
                         "alias": str(r.get("alias", "")), "canonical": str(r.get("canonical", "")),
                         "recorded_at": str(r.get("recorded_at", "") or now)},
                        "import-applied", table)
               for r in rows if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("alias")]
        emit(ops + (canon_ops() if final else []) + [receipt(part, len(ops))])

    if table in REJECT_DIM:
        dim = REJECT_DIM[table]
        ops = [store_op({"operation": "reject_pair", "table": dim[0], "column": dim[1],
                         "left": str(r.get("left_value", "")),
                         "right": str(r.get("right_value", "")),
                         "recorded_at": str(r.get("recorded_at", "") or now)},
                        "import-applied", table)
               for r in rows if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("left_value")]
        emit(ops + (canon_ops() if final else []) + [receipt(part, len(ops))])

    # A keyed content table. Two questions have to be answered together -- what
    # the part carries and what this store already has -- and a stateless cell
    # can hold ONE store result set at a time, so both are parked under one key
    # and read back in a single select. The two ops leave in the same hop under
    # DIFFERENT phases: their replies are told apart by the phase, never by the
    # order they come back in.
    keycols = KEYS[table]
    emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": SCRATCH,
                    "row": {"key": run, "kind": "part", "created_at": now,
                            "payload": json.dumps(part)}}, "import-probe", table),
          # The key columns of the WHOLE table, deliberately without a `where …
          # in [ids]`: an id list of the part's length would be bound as one SQL
          # parameter each, so the shape of the probe would carry a row ceiling
          # nobody declared. A few columns of one table is the cheaper read anyway.
          store_op({"operation": "select", "table": table, "columns": keycols},
                   "import-known", table)])

if phase == "import-probe":
    park()  # the echo of the parked part

if phase == "import-known" and op == "select":
    if err:
        refuse("import_probe_failed",
               "import aborted: probing %s for rows already present failed with %s (%s). "
               "Without that answer an import can only duplicate or skip blindly"
               % (table_ctx, err, first_text(d)))
    emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": SCRATCH,
                    "row": {"key": run, "kind": "known", "created_at": now,
                            "payload": json.dumps(rows_of(d))}}, "import-merge", table_ctx)])

if phase == "import-merge" and op == "insert":
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": SCRATCH,
                    "columns": ["key", "kind", "payload"], "where": {"key": run}},
                   "import-apply", table_ctx)])

if phase == "import-apply" and op == "select":
    part_row, known_row = None, None
    for r in rows_of(d):
        if r.get("kind") == "part":
            part_row = r
        elif r.get("kind") == "known":
            known_row = r
    if part_row is None or known_row is None:
        park()
    try:
        part = json.loads(part_row.get("payload") or "{}")
        known = json.loads(known_row.get("payload") or "[]")
    except Exception:
        park()
    table = str(part.get("table") or "")
    if table not in KEYS:
        park()
    keycols = KEYS[table]
    seen = {key_of(r, keycols) for r in known if isinstance(r, dict)}
    ops, written = [], 0
    for row in rows_for_insert(table, part.get("rows") or []):
        k = key_of(row, keycols)
        if k in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(k)
        ops.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": table, "row": row},
                            "import-applied", table))
        written += 1
    if part.get("final"):
        ops += canon_ops()
    emit(ops + [receipt(part, written)])

if phase == "import-applied":
    if err:
        # A write that failed AFTER the receipt left. It cannot be undone, so it
        # is said out loud on the lane the caller already drains.
        refuse("import_write_failed",
               "import: a %s on %s failed with %s (%s). The transfer is incomplete and the "
               "same document has to be applied again -- which is safe, because applying it "
               "twice is what this lane guarantees"
               % (op, table_ctx, err, first_text(d)))
    park()

# Anything else -- an echo of a phase this cell has no branch for.
park()

description.purpose: The one cell that can hand this hive's curated record out as a versioned document, and take one back. `memory` produces and `affinity` decides -- so a member reborn with its whole memory and an empty record remembers everything it was told and knows nothing about who may be told what. The walk reads nine tables in a defined order and emits one `dump` part per table, schema declaration first, rows after it; the last part carries the completeness marker. The same cell reads a part back on `in_import`, and applying the same part twice leaves the same state.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with affinity@3.3.0 and is reached by the hive's own `in_export` / `in_import` lanes. A birth does not use this lane at all: write each part out as `store/seed/<table>.jsonl` and instantiate. What a seed cannot do is reach a hive that is ALREADY RUNNING, and that is the half this lane exists for.
description.not_in_scope: It transfers; it does not decide. There is no filter here, no audience test and no second opinion about an identity: the alias table travels and `canonical_name` is re-derived from it, which is a deterministic function of transferred data rather than a fresh judgement. It writes no files itself -- since GH #555 the STORE writes the seed set, through the substrate's `transfer` slot and inside the fence it declares in `params.transfer.base_path`; this cell names the directory and says when it is whole. And it does not carry the rate at which this installation delivered its identity packs: `pack_hash` and `sent_at` are blanked on the way in, so the receiving colony makes its own first delivery.
